score.rationale: Gastroparesis (impaired gastric emptying) is a severe, often permanent GI motility disorder that can require feeding tubes or surgical intervention. GLP-1 receptor agonists like dulaglutide have a direct mechanism: they delay gastric emptying as part of their glucose-control effect, but prolonged use can lead to chronic gastroparesis. Two recent PubMed studies (2025, 2026) document the FAERS signal, and the label is silent on the risk (event_in_warnings false). Most importantly, 114 litigation hits in a streamlined E.D. Pa. MDL (filed Jan 2026) validate the signal as an emerging mass tort. Biologic status (no true generic) preserves brand-manufacturer liability. The moderate PRR (193, not artifact-level) and sustained case counts support viability. This is a live, accelerating tort; pursue for Eli Lilly exposure.
